# ai-sdk-harness-network

The hosts the sandbox of an [AI SDK harness agent](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-harnesses/harness-agent) may reach, so that its network can be **closed to everything else**: trusted lists for the forges, package registries, toolchains, container registries and Linux archives of the whole ecosystem, the hosts of every `@ai-sdk/harness-*` runtime and of the model providers, and the functions that check and merge them — with those of a workspace and of plugins — into the network policy every sandbox package takes. ## At a glance A coding agent needs few hosts: its model's API, the registry its runtime installs from, the forge of its repository, the registries of the project's packages. Every sandbox package takes them as `allowedHosts` and lets nothing else through; every application ends up writing the same list. This package writes it once: ```ts import { harnessHosts, networkPolicy, trustedHosts } from 'ai-sdk-harness-network'; import { createSbxNetworkSandboxSession } from 'ai-sdk-sandbox-sbx'; const sandboxSession = await createSbxNetworkSandboxSession({ ports: [4000], networkPolicy: networkPolicy( trustedHosts('github', 'javascript'), // GitHub, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Bun, JSR, Deno, Node.js harnessHosts(harness.harnessId), // Claude Code: registry.npmjs.org, api.anthropic.com ['api.acme.dev'], // your own ), }); // { mode: 'custom', allowedHosts: ['*.githubusercontent.com', 'api.acme.dev', 'api.anthropic.com', …] } ``` | The sandbox tries to reach | With the policy above | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `git clone https://github.com/acme/widgets` | Allowed: `github.com` | | `pnpm install` | Allowed: `registry.npmjs.org` | | A release asset, a raw file of GitHub | Allowed: `*.githubusercontent.com`, where GitHub serves them | | The model API, for the agent's turn | Allowed: `api.anthropic.com` | | `curl https://example.com` | Refused by the sandbox's proxy | | `pip install requests` | Refused: Python was not listed (`trustedHosts('python')`) | ## Installation ```bash pnpm add ai-sdk-harness-network ``` No dependency, peer or runtime: it is lists of hosts and the functions that check them. It runs in the browser too, where a settings form checks the hosts a user types as your server does. ## Usage ### Trusted hosts `trustedHosts(...names)` gives the hosts of the services named, or of the groups of them, every service without any. `TRUSTED_HOSTS` holds them by service, `TRUSTED_GROUPS` the services of each group (— for a service in none): | Group | Service | Hosts | | ---------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `forges` | `github` | `github.com`, `api.github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `*.githubusercontent.com` | | | `gitlab` | `gitlab.com`, `registry.gitlab.com`, `cdn.registry.gitlab-static.net` | | | `bitbucket` | `bitbucket.org`, `api.bitbucket.org` | | | `codeberg` | `codeberg.org` | | `javascript` | `npm` | `registry.npmjs.org` | | | `yarn` | `registry.yarnpkg.com`, `repo.yarnpkg.com` | | | `pnpm` | `get.pnpm.io` | | | `bun` | `bun.sh` | | | `jsr` | `jsr.io`, `npm.jsr.io` | | | `deno` | `deno.land`, `dl.deno.land` | | | `nodejs` | `nodejs.org`, `unofficial-builds.nodejs.org` | | `python` | `pypi` | `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org` | | | `uv` | `astral.sh`, `releases.astral.sh` | | | `conda` | `conda.anaconda.org`, `repo.anaconda.com` | | | `cpython` | `www.python.org`, `bootstrap.pypa.io` | | `rust` | `crates` | `crates.io`, `index.crates.io`, `static.crates.io` | | | `rustup` | `sh.rustup.rs`, `static.rust-lang.org` | | — | `go` | `proxy.golang.org`, `storage.googleapis.com`, `sum.golang.org`, `go.dev`, `dl.google.com` | | `jvm` | `maven` | `repo.maven.apache.org`, `repo1.maven.org` | | | `google-maven` | `maven.google.com`, `dl.google.com` | | | `gradle` | `services.gradle.org`, `downloads.gradle.org`, `plugins.gradle.org`, `plugins-artifacts.gradle.org` | | — | `rubygems` | `rubygems.org`, `index.rubygems.org` | | — | `packagist` | `packagist.org`, `repo.packagist.org`, `getcomposer.org` | | `dotnet` | `nuget` | `api.nuget.org`, `www.nuget.org`, `globalcdn.nuget.org` | | | `dotnet-sdk` | `dot.net`, `builds.dotnet.microsoft.com` | | — | `pub` | `pub.dev`, `storage.googleapis.com` | | — | `hex` | `hex.pm`, `repo.hex.pm`, `builds.hex.pm` | | — | `cocoapods` | `cdn.cocoapods.org`, `trunk.cocoapods.org` | | — | `swift` | `download.swift.org` | | — | `cran` | `cloud.r-project.org`, `cran.r-project.org` | | — | `hackage` | `hackage.haskell.org`, `downloads.haskell.org`, `get-ghcup.haskell.org` | | — | `cpan` | `www.cpan.org`, `cpan.metacpan.org`, `fastapi.metacpan.org` | | — | `zig` | `ziglang.org` | | `infrastructure` | `terraform` | `registry.terraform.io`, `releases.hashicorp.com` | | | `opentofu` | `registry.opentofu.org` | | | `helm` | `get.helm.sh` | | | `kubernetes` | `dl.k8s.io`, `registry.k8s.io`, `*.pkg.dev` | | `containers` | `docker-hub` | `registry-1.docker.io`, `auth.docker.io`, `production.cloudfront.docker.com`, `production.cloudflare.docker.com` | | | `ghcr` | `ghcr.io`, `pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com` | | | `quay` | `quay.io`, `*.quay.io` | | | `mcr` | `mcr.microsoft.com`, `*.data.mcr.microsoft.com` | | | `gcr` | `gcr.io`, `*.pkg.dev` | | `linux` | `debian` | `deb.debian.org`, `security.debian.org` | | | `ubuntu` | `archive.ubuntu.com`, `security.ubuntu.com`, `ports.ubuntu.com` | | | `alpine` | `dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org` | Each list names the hosts its default tool reaches, redirects followed: Gradle's distributions, uv, pnpm, Bun and OpenTofu's providers download from GitHub's releases (`github`), Go's module proxy from Cloud Storage. And the domain beside its `*.` wildcard: whether `*.example.com` covers `example.com` itself differs from one sandbox to another (microsandbox's does, srt's does not). `test/presets.e2e-spec.ts` fetches from each service, a Docker Hub image included, in a Docker Sandbox closed to all but `trustedHosts()`, and checks the proxy refused nothing. Some services rely on hosts shared with everyone: `storage.googleapis.com` (Go, Dart and Flutter), `dl.google.com`, `*.pkg.dev`. A sandbox that reaches them reaches any public bucket or registry there: name the services a project needs rather than all of them when that matters. ### The harness's own hosts `harnessHosts(harnessId, options?)` gives the hosts the harness's runtime reaches from the sandbox, by the `harnessId` of its adapter: where it installs, its own service, and the API of its models' provider. `HARNESS_NETWORK` holds them, read from each adapter — the packages it installs, the hosts its credentials are brokered to — and from each runtime's network documentation: | Harness | Installs from | Its service | Its provider | Optional | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `claude-code` | `registry.npmjs.org` | | `anthropic` | `http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com`, `browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com` (telemetry, errors) | | `codex` | `registry.npmjs.org` | | `openai`, `chatgpt` | | | `opencode` | `registry.npmjs.org` | | none: name one | `models.dev` (its list of models) | | `deepagents` | `registry.npmjs.org` | | `anthropic` | | | `cursor` | `cursor.com`, `downloads.cursor.com` | `*.cursor.sh` | | | | `github-copilot` | `registry.npmjs.org` | `github.com`, `api.github.com`, `api.githubcopilot.com`, `*.githubcopilot.com` | | `collector.github.com`, `copilot-telemetry.githubusercontent.com`, `default.exp-tas.com` | | `grok-build` | `registry.npmjs.org` | `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com` (a subscription) | `xai` | `code.grok.com`, `assets.grok.com` | | `cline`, `pi`, `fx` | — | — | — | They run on your server, the sandbox their file system and shell only: it reaches nothing | - `provider` takes another provider in place of the harness's own: `harnessHosts('claude-code', { provider: 'gateway' })` for the Vercel AI Gateway, `{ provider: 'amazon-bedrock', region: 'eu-west-3' }`, `{ provider: 'google-vertex', region: 'europe-west1' }`. OpenCode has no provider of its own: name it. - `optional: true` adds what a turn does without: refused, the runtime carries on. Most runtimes turn it off in their settings (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` for Claude Code, `--disable-client-telemetry` for Copilot). - `install: false` leaves out where the runtime installs from, for a sandbox started from a template that holds it. - Codex calls `api.openai.com` with an API key and `chatgpt.com` with a ChatGPT sign-in; Claude Code and Codex refresh a subscription's token on your server, never in the sandbox. - An ACP agent (`@ai-sdk/harness-acp`) has the id you give it and the hosts of the agent you install: list them, beside `registry.npmjs.org` where its bridge installs from. A harness the package does not know gives none. ### Model providers `providerHosts(provider, location?)` gives the hosts of a provider's API, by the name of its AI SDK provider package (`@ai-sdk/`): the default `baseURL` of that package. `PROVIDER_HOSTS` holds those whose host is the same for everyone: | Provider | Hosts | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `anthropic`, `openai`, `chatgpt` (a ChatGPT sign-in), `google` (Gemini API), `xai`, `mistral`, `groq`, `deepseek`, `cohere`, `perplexity`, `togetherai`, `fireworks`, `cerebras`, `deepinfra`, `baseten`, `huggingface`, `moonshotai`, `zai`, `alibaba`, `minimax`, `bytedance`, `gmicloud` | the API host of each: `api.anthropic.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `router.huggingface.co`… | | `gateway` (Vercel AI Gateway), `openrouter`, `ollama` (Ollama's cloud), `github-copilot` | `ai-gateway.vercel.sh`, `openrouter.ai`, `ollama.com`, `api.githubcopilot.com` | | `google-vertex`, `{ region }`: a region, or `global` (the default), `us`, `eu` | `-aiplatform.googleapis.com`, `aiplatform.googleapis.com` or `aiplatform..rep.googleapis.com`, and `oauth2.googleapis.com` for a service account's token | | `amazon-bedrock`, `{ region }` (required) | `bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com` | | `azure`, `{ resource }`: your resource, any without it | `.openai.azure.com`, `.services.ai.azure.com` | A region or a resource is a label of a host name: anything else throws. A provider the package does not know gives none. ### With a workspace and plugins [`ai-sdk-harness-workspace`](https://ai-sdk-harness.pages.dev/docs/packages/harness-workspace) names the hosts it fetches the repositories from, and [`ai-sdk-harness-plugins`](https://ai-sdk-harness.pages.dev/docs/packages/harness-plugins) those the selected plugins reach from the sandbox. Merge them with the presets: ```ts import { harnessHosts, networkPolicy, trustedHosts } from 'ai-sdk-harness-network'; const policy = networkPolicy( trustedHosts('javascript'), harnessHosts('claude-code'), await workspace.hosts({ sessionId }), // ['github.com'] catalog.hosts(selection).sandbox, // ['mcp.example.com', 'registry.npmjs.org'] ); ``` The same list goes to every sandbox package, under the name it takes: | Package | Where the hosts go | | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ai-sdk-sandbox-sbx` | `networkPolicy` at creation, `setNetworkPolicy()` while it runs | | `ai-sdk-sandbox-microsandbox` | `networkPolicy` at creation | | `ai-sdk-sandbox-cloud-run` | `allowedHosts`, on top of the service's `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and `setNetworkPolicy()` | | `ai-sdk-sandbox-runtime` | `allowedDomains` at creation (`allowedHosts(...)`), and `setNetworkPolicy()` | ### Checking hosts `allowedHosts(...lists)` returns the hosts of the lists, in lower case, each once and sorted; `networkPolicy(...lists)` wraps them in `{ mode: 'custom', allowedHosts }`. Both throw an `InvalidHostError`, which names the host, for one `isAllowedHost(host)` refuses: - a host name, `api.github.com`, or `*.` for the subdomains of a domain of two labels at least, `*.githubusercontent.com`; - no scheme, path nor port: a network policy allows a host on every port; - never `*` alone nor `*.com`, which would open the whole network. ```ts import { InvalidHostError, isAllowedHost, networkPolicy, trustedHosts, } from 'ai-sdk-harness-network'; isAllowedHost('*.example.dev'); // true isAllowedHost('https://example.dev'); // false try { networkPolicy(trustedHosts('javascript'), settings.extraHosts); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof InvalidHostError) console.error(`Not a host: ${error.host}`); } ``` ## Reference | Export | What it is | | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `networkPolicy(...)` | `{ mode: 'custom', allowedHosts }` from lists of hosts, checked and merged | | `allowedHosts(...)` | The hosts of lists, checked, in lower case, unique and sorted | | `isAllowedHost(host)` | Whether a network policy takes `host` | | `trustedHosts(...)` | The hosts of services or groups (`TrustedService`, `TrustedGroup`), or of all | | `TRUSTED_HOSTS` | The trusted hosts, by service | | `TRUSTED_GROUPS` | The services of each ecosystem | | `harnessHosts(id, options?)` | The hosts of a harness's runtime, by its `harnessId` (`HarnessHostsOptions`) | | `HARNESS_NETWORK` | What each harness the package knows reaches (`KnownHarness`, `HarnessNetwork`) | | `providerHosts(provider)` | The hosts of a model provider's API (`ModelProvider`, `ProviderLocation`) | | `PROVIDER_HOSTS` | The hosts of the providers whose host is the same for everyone (`FixedProvider`) | | `InvalidHostError` | Thrown for a host a network policy cannot take; its `host` is the one given | ## Limitations - The hosts of each harness belong with its adapter (`@ai-sdk/harness-*`), and those of each provider with its package: none publishes them yet. `HARNESS_NETWORK` and `PROVIDER_HOSTS` stand in for them, and follow the runtimes and the providers as they change. - `test/presets.e2e-spec.ts` runs real turns of Claude Code and Codex only; the other runtimes' hosts come from their adapters and documentation. - A registry set in a project's own configuration (`.npmrc`, a mirror, a private index) is not known: add its host. So are Fedora's mirrors, which vary from one download to the next, and Amazon ECR Public, whose layers come from an opaque CloudFront host. - A wildcard's reach depends on the sandbox: list a domain beside its `*.` wildcard when you need both. ## Development ```bash pnpm --filter ai-sdk-harness-network test pnpm --filter ai-sdk-harness-network test:e2e # Docker Sandboxes, Claude Code and Codex credentials ``` ## License MIT

# ai-sdk-harness-network

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- 55917d0: First release: the hosts the sandbox of a harness agent may reach, so that its network can be closed to everything else.
  
  - `trustedHosts(...names)` gives the hosts of services — forges (`github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `codeberg`), package registries and toolchains (`npm`, `yarn`, `jsr`, `deno`, `pypi`, `uv`, `conda`, `crates`, `rustup`, `go`, `maven`, `gradle`, `rubygems`, `packagist`, `nuget`, `pub`, `hex`…), infrastructure (`terraform`, `helm`, `kubernetes`), container registries (`docker-hub`, `ghcr`, `quay`, `mcr`, `gcr`) and Linux archives (`debian`, `ubuntu`, `alpine`) — or of groups of them (`'javascript'`, `'python'`, `'containers'`…), every service without any (`TRUSTED_HOSTS`, `TRUSTED_GROUPS`).
  - `harnessHosts(harness.harnessId, options?)` gives where each `@ai-sdk/harness-*` runtime installs from, its own service and its provider's API (`HARNESS_NETWORK`); `provider` takes another provider, `optional` adds telemetry and the like.
  - `providerHosts(provider, { region, resource })` gives the API hosts of the model providers of the AI SDK, Vertex AI, Bedrock and Azure by region or resource (`PROVIDER_HOSTS`).
  - `networkPolicy(...lists)` checks and merges them, with those of a workspace and of plugins, into `{ mode: 'custom', allowedHosts }`. `isAllowedHost()` and `InvalidHostError` refuse what a network policy cannot take: a scheme, a path, a port, `*` or `*.com`.
